sections.title: SURVEY BASIS
sections.body:
**Archive interval:** Wet-season and dry-season remote-imagery comparison with two limited ground-control visits

**Instrumentation:** Multispectral image set, soil-conductivity sled, shallow magnetometer array, and manual surface profile

**Study boundary:** A coded floodplain sector containing repeated linear relief and discontinuous vegetation bands.

sections.title: OBSERVED VARIANCE
sections.body:
**Geometric response:** Twenty-seven linear segments retained a common 3.6-metre spacing despite crossing present drainage and cultivation boundaries. Eleven terminated at near-right-angle returns.

**Subsurface response:** Shallow conductivity and magnetic gradients followed selected segments but did not identify masonry, continuous metal, or a modern pipe network.

**Seasonal behavior:** Vegetation contrast reversed between wet and dry observations while the geometric boundary remained stable.

sections.title: INTERPRETIVE LIMITS
sections.body:
**Ordinary explanations retained:** Historic drainage, former planting beds, buried combustion features, and repeated soil compaction can account for most observations.

**Unresolved point:** Available land-use material does not explain the full spacing pattern or its continuity across later surface changes. No age, builder, or original function is assigned.

sections.title: DISPOSITION
sections.body:
**Finding:** Persistent surface pattern of possible anthropogenic origin; source and age undetermined

**Action:** Preserve non-invasive baselines. Intrusive work requires a separate archaeological and land-access review.

**Hazard status:** No field hazard above ordinary floodplain conditions was established.
